content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): lifts the 14:00–17:15 window to 80.8%, just over the 80% target, at zero extra cost, but payments stays below target at 76.6%.","why":"The payments surge looks driven by the 08:35 UPI cashback push (MKT-2026-409), with calls up to +72% at 09:15 and service level down to 49%. Confidence is medium because the 08:00 bump came before the push. Doing nothing predicts 79.9% for the window, just under target. P1 delays payments breaks 14:00–15:00 by 45 minutes, runs IVR callback on payments 14:00–16:00, and moves 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:00–16:00. That gives 80.8% overall and cuts abandons from 5.2% to 4.8%, with no extra cost and no policy issues. General still improves slightly, from 87.2% to 88.0%. The rest of the day is predicted at 86.6%.","trade_offs":["P1 clears the target only narrowly (80.8%), and payments stays at 76.6%. Customers on the affected queue will still wait longer than target.","P2 (₹1,551) reaches 84.6% overall and 80.7% on payments, with 3.5% abandons. It uses chat deflection aimed at the campaign-driven reasons and cancels payments coaching 15:30–16:00.","P3 (₹2,631) gives the strongest recovery: 88.1% overall, 85.0% on payments and 2.6% abandons. It needs overtime for 14 agents and cancels coaching.","P4 (₹1,080) reaches 83.8% overall but only 78.9% on payments. It also delays breaks on both queues, which touches general staff unnecessarily.","P1 moves 4 agents out of general for an hour. General is still predicted at 88.0%, so the risk to that queue is low."],"watch":"Track payments service level and abandons from 14:00. The margin over 80% is only 0.8 points, so if payments volume runs above forecast (for example, a second campaign push), be ready to step up to P2's chat deflection on refund_status and payment_status_enquiry. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
